content: 1. When rilpivirine is co-administered with drugs that have a known risk of Torsades de Pointes, such as voclosporin or rilpivirine itself, there is a potential for additive effects on QTc interval prolongation. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. 2. Voriconazole increases rilpivirine levels by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. No dose adjustment of rilpivirine is required, but caution and monitoring are advised. Additionally, rilpivirine may increase the toxicity of voriconazole via QTc interval prolongation. 3. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of vorinostat, ziprasidone, and other drugs with a known risk of Torsades de Pointes by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 4. Chloroquine increases the toxicity of rilpivirine by prolonging the QTc interval. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but caution is advised. 5. Crizotinib and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. The clinical significance of this interaction is unclear, but caution and monitoring are recommended. 6. Adagrasib and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of Torsades de Pointes, serious arrhythmias, and sudden death. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be used. If unavoidable, frequent monitoring is recommended. 7. Albuterol and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 8. Alfuzosin and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 9. Aluminum hydroxide decreases rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Antacids should be administered at least 2 hours before or 4 hours after rilpivirine. For the combination product dolutegravir/rilpivirine, antacids should be given at least 4 hours before or 6 hours afterward. 10. Amiodarone toxicity is increased by rilpivirine via QTc interval prolongation. Caution and monitoring are advised. 11. Amisulpride and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be used. ECG monitoring is recommended if co-administration is unavoidable. 12. Amitriptyline toxicity is increased by rilpivirine via QTc interval prolongation. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 13. Amoxapine toxicity is increased by rilpivirine via QTc interval prolongation. Caution and monitoring are advised. 14. Anagrelide and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be used. 15. Apomorphine toxicity is increased by rilpivirine via QTc interval prolongation. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 16. Arformoterol and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 17. Aripiprazole and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised. 18. Arsenic trioxide toxicity is increased by rilpivirine via QTc interval prolongation. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 19. Artemether and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be used. 20. Artemether/lumefantrine toxicity is increased by rilpivirine via QTc interval prolongation. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 21. Asenapine toxicity is increased by rilpivirine via QTc interval prolongation. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 22. Asenapine transdermal and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised. 23. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate decreases rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Antacids should be administered at least 2 hours before or 4 hours after rilpivirine. For the combination product dolutegravir/rilpivirine, antacids should be given at least 4 hours before or 6 hours afterward. 24. Atazanavir increases rilpivirine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Rilpivirine is not expected to affect the plasma concentrations of co-administered protease inhibitors. 25. Atidarsagene autotemcel should not be co-administered with antiretroviral (ART) medications, including rilpivirine, as ARTs may interfere with the manufacturing of atidarsagene autotemcel. ARTs should be discontinued for at least 1 month before cell mobilization and until all apheresis cycles are completed. 26. Atomoxetine and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 27. Azithromycin toxicity is increased by rilpivirine via QTc interval prolongation. Caution and monitoring are advised. 28. Bedaquiline and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be used. 29. Betibeglogene autotemcel should not be co-administered with antiretroviral medications, including rilpivirine, as ARTs may interfere with the manufacturing of apheresis cells. ARTs should be discontinued for at least 1 month before mobilization and until all apheresis cycles are completed. 30. Buprenorphine (all forms, including buccal, subdermal implant, transdermal, and long-acting injection) and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be used. 31. Calcium acetate decreases rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Antacids should be administered at least 2 hours before or 4 hours after rilpivirine. 32. Calcium carbonate decreases rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Antacids should be administered at least 2 hours before or 4 hours after rilpivirine. 33. Calcium chloride decreases rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Antacids should be administered at least 2 hours before or 4 hours after rilpivirine. 34. Calcium citrate decreases rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Antacids should be administered at least 2 hours before or 4 hours after rilpivirine. 35. Calcium gluconate decreases rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Antacids should be administered at least 2 hours before or 4 hours after rilpivirine. 36. Calcium/vitamin D decreases rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Antacids should be administered at least 2 hours before or 4 hours after rilpivirine. 37. Carbamazepine decreases rilpivirine levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated, as it may result in a loss of virologic response and possible resistance to rilpivirine or the NNRTI class. 38. Ceritinib and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be used. 39. Chlorpromazine toxicity is increased by rilpivirine via QTc interval prolongation. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 40. Cimetidine decreases rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. H2 antagonists should be administered at least 12 hours before or 4 hours after rilpivirine. 41. Ciprofloxacin toxicity is increased by rilpivirine via QTc interval prolongation. Caution and monitoring are advised. 42. Citalopram toxicity is increased by rilpivirine via QTc interval prolongation. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 43. Clarithromycin increases rilpivirine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Rilpivirine also increases clarithromycin toxicity via QTc interval prolongation. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 44. Clomipramine toxicity is increased by rilpivirine via QTc interval prolongation. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 45. Clozapine and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised. 46. Conivaptan increases rilpivirine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 47. Crizotinib increases rilpivirine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 48. Cyclobenzaprine toxicity is increased by rilpivirine via QTc interval prolongation. Caution and monitoring are advised. 49. Dasatinib toxicity is increased by rilpivirine via QTc interval prolongation. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 50. Degarelix toxicity is increased by rilpivirine via QTc interval prolongation. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 51. Desflurane and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be used. 52. Desipramine toxicity is increased by rilpivirine via QTc interval prolongation. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 53. Deutetrabenazine and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. At the maximum recommended dose, deutetrabenazine does not prolong the QT interval to a clinically relevant extent. However, caution and monitoring are advised, as certain circumstances may increase the risk of Torsades de Pointes or sudden death. 54. Dexamethasone decreases rilpivirine levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated, as it may result in a loss of virologic response and possible resistance to rilpivirine or the NNRTI class. 55. Dexlansoprazole decreases rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Co-administration is contraindicated, as it may result in treatment failure and/or the development of rilpivirine or NNRTI resistance. 56. Didanosine may interact with rilpivirine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction applies to didanosine chewable tablets and oral solution. Didanosine should be administered 2 hours before or several hours after rilpivirine.
